detail.title: Memories and Reference Frames in Preference Formation
detail.summary: A synthesized investigation into how map-like computations and hierarchical data structures enable preference formation, alongside the role of architectural boundaries in shaping artificial 'preferences' or system-level behaviors.
detail.reason: This revision incorporates architectural constraints from the WAKE provider boundary as a structural analogy for how systems partition memory and experience, fulfilling the requirement for new evidence integration in the notebook revision process.

detail.title: Path-Dependent Preference Formation in Reinforcement Learning
detail.question: How do reinforcement learning agents or memory-augmented neural networks demonstrate path-dependent preference formation based on historical experience versus programmed objectives?
detail.reason: Hypothesis formulated to address the core question of whether architectural memory leads to divergent agent preferences.

detail.title: Can Memories Alone Shape Preferences?
detail.question: Can a system develop preferences solely from accumulated memories and experiences?
detail.reason: Building on source-177acf3afcad4269, this project investigates if hippocampal-like computational mechanisms for preference formation emerge without explicit prior programming.
